name: Flip a bottle consistently
blurb: The 2016 playground obsession, and a genuine physics lesson: the water fill level changes the moment of inertia and determines whether it lands.
gear: A plastic bottle with a cap
steps: Fill the bottle about one third with water. This is the ratio that lets the water shift and damp the landing.
Hold it by the neck and toss with a gentle upward flick, aiming for exactly one rotation.
Keep the release consistent — same height, same spin, same force every time.
Watch how the water sloshes: too full and it will not settle, too empty and it bounces.
Practise on a hard flat surface, then vary the surface.
Progress to the cap landing, which needs less rotation and a softer release.
tips: One rotation, not one and a half. Most failures are over-spinning.
Fill level is the biggest variable. Tune it before blaming your throw.
proof: Eight successful landings out of ten from your standard setup.
